correctness.rationale: The square-zero binomial expansion gives N_B^n=εS(B) and N_B^(n+j)=εS(B)J_n^j, where S(B)=Σ J_n^i B J_n^(n−1−i). The commutator telescopes, so S(B) lies in the Jordan-block centralizer. Conversely the map B↦S(B) is onto that n-dimensional Toeplitz algebra because E_(n,k+1) maps to J_n^k. Hence each coefficient vector has q^(n²−n) preimages, and the least nonzero Toeplitz coefficient determines the exact vanishing power. Fresh independent replay verified the basis-map identity for n≤5 and directly enumerated the distributions (1,2), (2,2), (3,2), and (2,3), matching the theorem exactly.

value.rationale: A single nilpotent Jordan block is the canonical indecomposable fiber for studying square-zero matrix lifts. The theorem does not merely sharpen an upper bound: it completely resolves every possible lifted index and its field-uniform multiplicity, giving a natural exact benchmark for more complicated nilpotent Jordan types.

final_claim: For every prime power q and nilpotent Jordan block J_n, the lifts J_n+εB over the dual-number ring have nilpotency indices exactly n through 2n, with q^(n²−n) lifts of index n and (q−1)q^(n²−n+j−1) lifts of index n+j for 1≤j≤n; in particular the doubled index occurs with probability 1−q⁻¹.
limitations: The exact distribution is for a single Jordan block; several-block nilpotent real parts may behave differently.
Counting uses finiteness of the base field, though the structural power formula is field-independent.
